s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive hip pain with night pain and weight loss, associated with limited range of motion and synovitis
salient_findings: Progressive left hip pain radiating to the anterior thigh
Severe night pain
Weight loss and anorexia
Reduced range of motion of the left hip with spasms and tenderness
Synovitis and marrow edema on MRI
key_facts: 1-year history of progressive left hip pain
Pain radiates to the anterior thigh
Pain is severe at night
Associated with weight loss and anorexia
No history of trauma
Antalgic gait
Reduced range of motion of the left hip in all planes
Tenderness deep in the left groin
Normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein
Unremarkable pelvic radiograph
MRI shows synovitis and marrow edema without fracture
No clinical improvement with empirical anti-tubercular therapy
Open synovial biopsy shows mild to moderate chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates
Negative cultures and unremarkable rheumatologic evaluation

shortlist.label: Chronic osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hip pain with night pain and weight loss, associated with synovitis and marrow edema

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Severe night pain and weight loss, associated with a well-defined lesion in the femoral head

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive hip pain with limited range of motion, associated with a sclerotic rim and marrow edema

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic synovitis with lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates, associated with joint effusion and synovitis

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring hip pain with synovitis and marrow edema, despite normal laboratory studies

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive hip pain, night pain, and weight loss, along with imaging findings of synovitis, marrow edema, and a well-defined lesion with a sclerotic rim, are consistent with chronic osteomyelitis. The lack of response to anti-tubercular therapy and negative cultures do not rule out this diagnosis, as chronic osteomyelitis can be caused by a variety of organisms and may not always be culture-positive.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Ewing's sarcoma could explain the night pain and weight loss, the imaging findings and biopsy results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Osteosarcoma is unlikely given the patient's age and the lack of aggressive features on imaging.

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: PVNS typically presents with joint effusion and synovitis, but the imaging findings in this case suggest a more localized process.

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: CRMO is a diagnosis of exclusion and typically presents with multiple sites of involvement, which is not the case here.
